title: 1932–33 National Hurling League
text:
{{Short description|Sixth season of the National Hurling League}} {{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}} {{Infobox GAA League |league = 1932–33 National Hurling League |image = |dates = 18 September 1932 – 9 April 1933 |teams = 10 |team1 = Kilkenny |captain1 = |manager1 = |titles = 1st |team2 = |captain2 = |manager2 = |oneb = |twoa = |twob = |threea = |threeb = |previous = [[1930–31 National Hurling League|1930–31]] |next = [[1933–34 National Hurling League|1933–34]] }} The '''1932–33 National Hurling League''' was the sixth season of the [[National Hurling League]]. ==Format== The ten participating teams were [[Clare GAA|Clare]], [[Cork GAA|Cork]], [[Dublin GAA|Dublin]], [[Galway GAA|Galway]], [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]], [[Laois GAA|Laois]], [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]], [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]], [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] and [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] who were divided into two divisions and agreed to play a four-game format whereby each team would play each of their five rivals once with two points awarded for a win and one point awarded for a drawn game. The two teams with the most points in each division at the completion of the season would play a final to decide the National Hurling League champions. ==National Hurling League== {{Infobox football league season |competition=[[National Hurling League]] |season=1932-33 |winners=[[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]]
1st National League title

On 9 April 1933, [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] won the title after a 3-8 to 1-3 win over [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] in the final.
